solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crossing heather pass odd-looking little trees

indicators.note: crossing here means the rearranged letters straddle the heather, sitting either side of it
something odd-looking is out of shape, so the letters of pass are rearranged

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A walker crossing a heather-covered pass spots some strange-looking small trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Ling is a name for common heather; 'odd-looking' rearranges the pass, and 'Crossing' has that straddle the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Young trees not yet grown to full size are called saplings.

clue.text: Freckled little son being toilet-trained it seems!

parts.note: S is the usual short form for son
a child being toilet-trained is potty-trained, so the playful phrase suggests potty

explanation.surface: A small boy with freckles appears to be learning to use the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the whimsical step from toilet-training to the word POTTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin covered in freckles is marked with spots, hence spotty.

clue.text: Pair beginning to enjoy wonderful home — temporary one?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from enjoy

parts.note: fab is informal slang for wonderful

explanation.surface: A couple start to enjoy a lovely house, though perhaps it is only a stopgap.
explanation.definitionFit: Prefabricated houses were put up quickly in post-war Britain as stopgap housing, often meant to last only a few years.

clue.text: Passages sealed off at the top in British locations, say?

indicators.note: sealing off the top of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: aisles are passages between rows of seats

explanation.surface: Corridors closed at their upper end somewhere in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealed off at the top' removes the A at the head of AISLES, the passages; 'say?' warns that the definition is by example, the British Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Islands are places, and the British Isles are an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Maybe a jacket fellow's hung over part of chair

indicators.note: the fellow is draped over the chair part, so his letters wrap around it

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or fellow; the 's is read as 'is'
an arm is one part of an armchair

explanation.surface: A man's jacket has been slung over a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hung over' has the fellow draped around the chair part, not a sense of being hungover.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket is one example of an item of clothing.

clue.text: Bad feeling from bishop leaving a cloud

indicators.note: the bishop leaving the cloud means his letter is taken out of it

parts.note: a nimbus is a rain cloud
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop departing under a cloud leaves resentment behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A nimbus is a rain cloud; 'leaving' takes the chess bishop out of it, with the A placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is hostility or ill will towards someone.

clue.text: Ruin a leg, having to run around with a sort of pain

indicators.note: running around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An athlete wrecks a leg by running and is left in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to run around' rearranges RUIN A LEG plus the later A.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp pain along the course of a nerve.

clue.text: Happy about university getting pounds — it should bear fruit

indicators.note: about means going around, so the merry letters surround the others

parts.note: merry means happy
LB is the abbreviation for pounds in weight

explanation.surface: A cheerful college gets cash, which ought to pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the happy word around university and pounds; 'getting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulberry is a tree grown for its dark berries.

clue.text: Like many an old record making one bad-tempered

definitions.meaning: old vinyl records often sound crackly from surface wear

explanation.definitionFit: Worn records crackle with scratches, and a scratchy person is irritable and touchy.

clue.text: Boss going about in old Rover

indicators.note: going about suggests the letters turning about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: The boss drives around in an old Rover car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' rearranges OLD ROVER; Rover is a British car make.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlord is a ruler with supreme power over others, a boss.

clue.text: Servant still left attending Queen

parts.note: but can mean still or nevertheless
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A servant still remains, waiting on the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household.

clue.text: Four members of that university set up in American state

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised and so read upwards
four letters taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Four people from a university are established in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four members of' takes HATU from 'that university' and 'set up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is a western US state whose capital is Salt Lake City.

clue.text: Ephemeral article is about to be submerged in river

indicators.note: being submerged in a river puts the pieces inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about indicates a turning round, so the letters of is are reversed

explanation.surface: Something short-lived is about to sink beneath a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is an English river; 'about' turns round 'is', and 'to be submerged in' sinks both pieces into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something lasting only a short time.

clue.text: Vigilant husband of Victoria, not British

indicators.note: not British means the abbreviation for British is dropped

parts.note: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria's watchful consort, who was not British-born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the B from ALBERT; Albert was indeed German-born.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vigilant means watchful and on guard, synonyms of alert.

clue.text: Get rid of mould

definitions.meaning: to throw off or discard, as a snake sheds its skin
a form into which molten metal is poured

explanation.definitionFit: Cast means to shed or throw off, and also a mould for shaping metal or plaster.

clue.text: Liveliness of one maiden in a race

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a nation can mean a people or race
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A single young woman in a race shows great spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I and M inside A and NATION; a maiden is an over without runs in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means vivacity, spirit or liveliness.

clue.text: Artist exhibiting pig paintings maybe by entrance to hotel

parts.note: a hog is a pig
paintings are an example of art

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A painter shows pictures of pigs beside a hotel doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was an 18th-century English painter and satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth is a famous English painter and engraver.

clue.text: Living in trees in hole between a river and a lake

indicators.note: the hole is placed between the first pair and the second pair of pieces

parts.note: a bore is a hole drilled out

explanation.surface: A creature dwells in a hollow between a river and a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts BORE between A R and A L.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal means tree-dwelling, as of monkeys or squirrels.

clue.text: Mum to hum softly when chewing a biscuit

parts.note: ma is a word for mum

indicators.note: chewing means holding something in the mouth, so the letters close around the A

parts.note: to croon is to sing or hum softly

explanation.surface: Mother hums gently while munching a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' puts A inside CROON.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a sweet almond or coconut biscuit.

clue.text: University library offers facility for this

definitions.meaning: the University of ... is in the English town of ...
libraries provide books and space for perusing them

explanation.definitionFit: Reading is an English university town, and perusing books is what a library offers.

clue.text: Member of film crew to complain endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to gripe is to complain

explanation.surface: A film crew member keeps grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final E of GRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is a technician on a film set who handles cameras and rigging.

clue.text: Elegant fabric concealing article

indicators.note: concealing means holding something hidden inside

parts.note: net is a mesh fabric
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A stylish fabric hides some item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts A inside NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat can mean smart, tidy and elegant in appearance.

clue.text: Writer standing on head to make fine adjustments to heavenly body

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing on its head means the word is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to tune is to adjust finely

explanation.surface: An author stands on their head to fine-tune a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing on head' turns PEN into NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun, a heavenly body.

clue.text: The French profiteer is released from prison

parts.note: le is French for the
a tout resells tickets at inflated prices for profit

explanation.surface: A French racketeer has been freed from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: A ticket tout is a British term for someone reselling tickets at a profit, a scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: Let out is a phrasal verb meaning freed or released, as a prisoner is.

clue.text: Waxy stuff coming from master, old

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wax that has come from an old master's painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterols are waxy steroid alcohols such as cholesterol.

clue.text: US city given prestigious UK award — gosh!

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
aha is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: An American city receives a top British honour, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska.

clue.text: Job wasn't quiet — it meant I worried about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the quiet piece
worried letters are fretted and shaken out of order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Job was not silent; it meant I fretted about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges IT MEANT I and 'about' puts it around P; the final 'it' is a link. The biblical Job was famous for his patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial patience of Job means the opposite trait is one he lacked.

clue.text: Those people taking priority over English subject

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking priority means coming above, so the first piece goes before

parts.note: them means those people

explanation.surface: Some people are favoured over English as a topic of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk or piece of work.

clue.text: Strange old sweetheart needs love, twitching

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
O is love, a zero score in tennis
a tic is a twitch

explanation.surface: An odd former partner needs affection and keeps twitching.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic means unusual, foreign or strange.

clue.text: Final words from a posh minister, one entertained by soldiers

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

indicators.note: entertained by means held within, so the soldiers' letters surround the one

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grand clergyman, put up by the troops, says goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' puts I inside OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Au revoir is the French farewell, words said on parting.

clue.text: London's No. 1 home — home given good protection

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its first

parts.note: in means at home
in again means at home

explanation.surface: London's best house, and a good house at that, gives shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lining is an inner layer that protects a garment or container.

clue.text: Support journalist established in China

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the friend

parts.note: china means mate, from rhyming slang china plate = mate, so a pal
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter backed by help settled in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is a base that supports a statue or column.
